deductions.evidence: Synthetic repair invoice INV-01: repair existing shelf, materials and labour GBP 80.00. No replacement or improvement. Tenant admits causing the break.
Synthetic quotation Q-02: repaint hallway GBP 120.00. Scuffs were present at check-in and did not worsen. No new damage.

claim.inspection: Synthetic check-in report, agreed by both parties: bedroom shelf intact; hallway paint already scuffed. Synthetic check-out report, agreed by both parties: bedroom shelf broken; hallway paint has similar scuffs.
claim.lease: The tenant must pay reasonable documented repair costs for damage caused by the tenant beyond ordinary wear. Ordinary wear and pre-existing damage are not deductible. Replacement must not improve the original condition.
claim.title: Synthetic demo · broken shelf and worn paint

response.statement: Synthetic tenant response: I agree these are our lease terms. I broke the shelf during my tenancy and agree with the GBP 80 repair invoice. The hallway scuffs were already present at check-in, did not worsen, and are ordinary wear. I dispute the GBP 120 repainting deduction.

findings.evidence_quote: Synthetic quotation Q-02: repaint hallway GBP 120.00. Scuffs were present at check-in and did not worsen. No new damage.
findings.lease_quote: Ordinary wear and pre-existing damage are not deductible.
findings.reason: The lease expressly excludes ordinary wear and pre-existing damage. The inspection and deduction evidence both say the hallway paint was already scuffed at check-in and similar at check-out, with no worsening or new damage. That supports no deductible damage and no tenant-caused deterioration. The quote does state a GBP 120 repainting amount, so the claimed cost itself is stated, but the underlying basis for deduction is not supported.
findings.tenant_quote: The hallway scuffs were already present at check-in, did not worsen, and are ordinary wear. I dispute the GBP 120 repainting deduction.

findings.evidence_quote: Synthetic repair invoice INV-01: repair existing shelf, materials and labour GBP 80.00. No replacement or improvement. Tenant admits causing the break.
findings.lease_quote: The tenant must pay reasonable documented repair costs for damage caused by the tenant beyond ordinary wear.
findings.reason: The lease expressly allows documented repair costs for tenant-caused damage beyond ordinary wear. Check-in says the shelf was intact and check-out says it was broken, supporting damage during the tenancy. The tenant expressly admits causing the break. The invoice supports a repair, not replacement or improvement, and states materials and labour of GBP 80.00.
findings.tenant_quote: I broke the shelf during my tenancy and agree with the GBP 80 repair invoice.

assessment.reason: Each deduction was assessed only against the lease and submitted evidence. The shelf repair is supported by the lease, inspection change from intact to broken, tenant admission, and a documented repair invoice without improvement. The hallway repainting is not supported because the lease excludes ordinary wear and pre-existing damage, and the records say the scuffs already existed and did not worsen.
